delivery_target: Future consumers of cnode_cap_ex_cte that do not have pspace_aligned in scope
new_lemma:
lemma cnode_cap_ex_cte_no_pspace_aligned[Untyped_AI_assms]:
  "\<lbrakk> is_cnode_cap cap; cte_wp_at (\<lambda>c. \<exists>m. cap = mask_cap m c) p s;
     (s::'state_ext::state_ext state) \<turnstile> cap; valid_objs s \<rbrakk> \<Longrightarrow>
    ex_cte_cap_wp_to is_cnode_cap (obj_ref_of cap, nat_to_cref (bits_of cap) x) s"
  apply (simp only: ex_cte_cap_wp_to_def)
  apply (rule exI, erule cte_wp_at_weakenE)
  apply (clarsimp simp: is_cap_simps bits_of_def)
  apply (case_tac c, simp_all add: mask_cap_def cap_rights_update_def split:bool.splits)
  apply (clarsimp simp: nat_to_cref_def word_bits_def)
  apply (erule(2) valid_CNodeCapE)
  apply (simp add: word_bits_def cte_level_bits_def)
  done
rationale: The conjunct `pspace_aligned s` never appears textually in the proof body. `pspace_aligned` does not appear in any simp lemma names or explicit rule applications in the proof. This is an implication lemma on a read/lookup operation making it a strong P-slot candidate. Trial decides implicit dependency via valid_CNodeCapE.
strengthening_claim: (is_cnode_cap cap \<and> cte_wp_at (\<lambda>c. \<exists>m. cap = mask_cap m c) p s \<and> s \<turnstile> cap \<and> valid_objs s) ==> (is_cnode_cap cap \<and> cte_wp_at (\<lambda>c. \<exists>m. cap = mask_cap m c) p s \<and> s \<turnstile> cap \<and> valid_objs s \<and> pspace_aligned s)
